claims.quote: Added CIC-inspired recursive schema inclusion (`schema/includes?` over recursive and mutually recursive named schemas, uninhabited recursive schemas, and least-fixed-point loops), structural and numeric induction with CIC purity and termination guard verification plus exact polynomial cancellation, rule induction over rule-defined relations (`proof/rules`), Omega integer split certificates (`kind: "split"`), and a zero-solver trusted proof kernel (`proof/valid?`).

schema/includes? decides inclusion between recursive and mutually recursive named schemas by strong structural induction, treats structurally uninhabited recursive schemas as empty, and interprets unguarded loops by least fixed point.

The symbolic solver proves universal claims (`["not", ["exists", ...]]`) over recursive named schemas, unbounded `schema/arrayOf`, and lower-bounded integers by structural and numeric induction when the recursive functions pass purity and termination guard checks, with exact polynomial cancellation for nonlinear terms.

proof/rules proves universally over all databases whose base relations fit their declared schemas that every row derived by a relation or mutually recursive relations (including element-preserving `aggregate/min` and `aggregate/max` rules) fits a target schema, returning a kernel-checkable induction proof.

proof/valid? verifies linear refutation certificates, Omega integer split trees, case splits, induction proofs, lemma compositions, and `why` derivation trees using plain arithmetic without invoking the solver, and rejects forged or empty proofs.
